$comment: The one definition of what counts as a DECLARED AI assistant in a commit message. Every runtime that reads commit messages for REWORK Proof loads this file and nothing else, so a commit reads the same from the Action, the App and the MCP server. Each `tools[].pattern` is a regular expression fragment written in the subset that JavaScript and Python evaluate identically: no lookbehind, no named groups, no flags inline. Matching is always case-insensitive. `patterns` are tried in order and the first hit is the verdict; `{{tools}}` expands to the alternation of every tool pattern. A match means the author DECLARED the tool in the message. No match means nothing was declared; it never means nothing was used.

tools.name: Devin
tools.note: Devin is also a common first name, so a bare `Devin` is not enough: the vendor login or address has to be there.

tools.name: Cline
tools.note: Cline is also a surname (a `Patsy Cline <patsy@example.com>` co-author is a person), so the word alone never counts: only the vendor address or login does.

tools.name: Jules
tools.note: Jules is also a first name; only the vendor login or address counts.

patterns.what: A Co-authored-by trailer naming one of the tools above, in any casing (`Co-Authored-By`, `Co-authored-by`, `co-authored-by`).
The `Claude-Session:` trailer Claude Code writes beside its co-author line.
The `Amp-Thread-ID:` trailer Amp writes beside its co-author line.
A `Generated with <tool>` or `Generated by <tool>` line, with or without a markdown link around the tool name. `Regenerated with build.js` is a human sentence about a script and does not count.
The robot-emoji form, `🤖 Generated ...`, which some tools write without naming themselves on the same line.
